testName: ICT3722 · Oracle user & privilege SQL · verified practice
sourceType: Practice based on older ICT3722 tutorial-solution topics and cross-checked with Oracle SQL documentation.
sourceLimitations: Recent full assessment wording is not reliably public. These tasks use verified Oracle syntax and course topics instead of inventing a current paper.

questions.text: Write an Oracle SQL statement that changes user `rthomas` to the new password `anew5password`.
questions.correctAnswer: ALTER USER rthomas IDENTIFIED BY anew5password;
questions.explanation:
Oracle changes a database user's password with `ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY ...` when the executing account has the required privilege (or the user changes their own password as permitted).

Student note: `ALTER USER` changes account properties; it does not grant table privileges.

questions.text: Grant user `rthomas` permission to query table `orders`, and allow that user to grant the same object privilege to another user.
questions.correctAnswer: GRANT SELECT ON orders TO rthomas WITH GRANT OPTION;
questions.explanation:
`GRANT SELECT ON orders` gives an object privilege on that table. `WITH GRANT OPTION` lets the grantee pass that object privilege to another user.

Student note: The grant option increases authority, so use it only when delegation is intended.

questions.text: Create an Oracle database user named `practice_user` with password `StrongPass7`.
questions.correctAnswer: CREATE USER practice_user IDENTIFIED BY StrongPass7;
questions.explanation:
`CREATE USER ... IDENTIFIED BY ...` creates the account and defines password authentication. Additional privileges such as CREATE SESSION are normally required before the user can log in.

Student note: Creating a user and giving that user privileges are separate steps.

questions.text: Grant `practice_user` the system privilege needed to create a database session.
aiRubric: Uses GRANT CREATE SESSION TO practice_user.
questions.explanation:
In Oracle, CREATE SESSION is the system privilege that permits a database user to establish a session.

Student note: Object privileges such as SELECT and system privileges such as CREATE SESSION solve different access-control needs.

questions.text: Revoke `SELECT` privilege on table `orders` from user `rthomas`.
questions.correctAnswer: REVOKE SELECT ON orders FROM rthomas;
aiRubric: Uses REVOKE SELECT ON orders FROM rthomas.
questions.explanation:
`REVOKE` removes a previously granted privilege. Here it removes rthomas's SELECT object privilege on orders.

Student note: GRANT adds privilege; REVOKE removes privilege.

questions.text: Explain the difference between an Oracle system privilege and an object privilege, and give one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: A system privilege authorises a database-level operation, such as CREATE SESSION or CREATE TABLE. An object privilege authorises an operation on a specific database object, such as SELECT ON orders or UPDATE ON customers.
aiRubric: Gives a valid system privilege example.
Gives a valid object privilege example tied to an object.
questions.explanation:
System privileges answer 'what kind of database operation may this account perform?'. Object privileges answer 'what may this account do to this specific table, view or other object?'.

Student note: If the SQL contains `ON table_name`, you are often looking at an object privilege.

questions.text: Write one Oracle query that shows `vendor_name`, `invoice_number` and `invoice_total` by joining `vendors` and `invoices` on `vendor_id`, then sorts the results from the highest invoice total to the lowest.
questions.correctAnswer:
SELECT v.vendor_name, i.invoice_number, i.invoice_total
FROM vendors v
JOIN invoices i ON i.vendor_id = v.vendor_id
ORDER BY i.invoice_total DESC;
aiRubric: Joins vendors to invoices using vendor_id.
Equivalent ANSI JOIN syntax is accepted.
questions.explanation:
The join combines related vendor and invoice rows through vendor_id. `ORDER BY ... DESC` then places the largest invoice totals first.

Student note: Build SQL in layers: SELECT columns → FROM/JOIN tables → ON relationship → ORDER BY result.
